themes_detail.label: Street infrastructure collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street Condition complaints spiked to 103 THIS WEEK versus a 13.4 weekly average—a 670% increase (z-score: 11.69)—signaling potential widespread pavement, pothole, or drainage failures across Parkchester/Soundview that demand immediate investigation and repair.
evidence: Street Condition complaints: 103 THIS WEEK vs. 13.4 weekly average (670% spike, z-score 11.69)
Concurrent Sewer complaints: 15 THIS WEEK vs. 3.6 weekly average (314% spike, z-score 5.89)—suggests underlying infrastructure failure
Street Sign - Damaged complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)—indicates physical deterioration across district
reporting_angles: Field survey: map and photograph worst-condition streets in Parkchester/Soundview to document deterioration patterns
Accountability angle: has NYCDOT prioritized this district for maintenance? What caused the sudden spike?
Infrastructure/sewer nexus: are failing sewers buckling streets, or vice versa? Interview NYC Department of Environmental Protection

themes_detail.label: Tree emergency unfolding
themes_detail.summary: Dead/Dying Tree complaints reached 7 LAST WEEK versus a 0.2 weekly average (2700% spike, z-score 15.59), while Damaged Tree complaints hit 6 THIS WEEK versus 0.6 average (860% spike)—indicating a widespread tree health crisis or recent storm damage across parks and streets.
evidence: Dead/Dying Tree complaints: 7 LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (2700% spike, z-score 15.59)
Damaged Tree complaints: 6 THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (860% spike, z-score 7.72)
Recurring CB budget request for 'new building or expansion in a park'—suggests park infrastructure has been neglected, including tree care
reporting_angles: Environmental health: interview Parks Department about why tree deaths are spiking. Recent weather events? Pest infestation? Deferred maintenance?
Public safety: are dead/damaged trees creating hazards for residents? Document location and height of at-risk trees
Community impact: focus on parks like Soundview Park—how are tree losses affecting green space and quality of life?

themes_detail.label: Street noise surge
themes_detail.summary: Street/Sidewalk Noise complaints jumped to 55 LAST WEEK versus a 7.0 weekly average (686% increase, z-score 13.71), indicating a sudden, acute noise disturbance—possibly construction, street events, or enforcement gap.
evidence: Street/Sidewalk Noise complaints: 55 LAST WEEK vs. 7.0 weekly average (686% spike, z-score 13.71)
Concurrent with Street Condition spike (103 complaints THIS WEEK), suggesting street work as possible cause
Residential Noise baseline remains high (2,387 complaints over 90 days), indicating chronic noise problem compounded by new source
reporting_angles: Source identification: are multiple construction projects, street fairs, or illegal loudspeaker use driving the spike?
311 data mapping: pinpoint which blocks are generating the most complaints to narrow source location
Enforcement gap: is NYPD responding to noise complaints? Interview precinct about enforcement resources

themes_detail.label: Park rule violations spike
themes_detail.summary: Violation of Park Rules complaints reached 10 LAST WEEK versus a 1.4 weekly average (627% increase, z-score 7.76), suggesting emerging public disorder, unsafe behavior, or inadequate park enforcement in district parks.
evidence: Violation of Park Rules: 10 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (627% spike, z-score 7.76)
Concurrent tree damage surge suggests possible vandalism or storm-driven access problems in parks
Recurring CB budget request for 'new or expanded park buildings' and 'expand street outreach'—indicates longstanding park management and safety concerns
reporting_angles: Park safety audit: what specific violations are being reported? Unlicensed vending, drug activity, trespassing, unsupervised youth?
Enforcement presence: interview Parks Enforcement Patrol about staffing and response times in Soundview and Parkchester parks
Community perception: talk to residents about feeling safe in district parks and whether visible disorder has increased

themes_detail.label: For-hire vehicle spike
themes_detail.summary: For Hire Vehicle Complaints spiked to 5 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a 1.6 weekly average (208% increase, z-score 6.97), suggesting a possible surge in unlicensed taxis, Uber/Lyft congestion, or traffic violations in the district.
evidence: For Hire Vehicle Complaint: 5 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 1.6 weekly average (208% spike, z-score 6.97)
Baseline illegal parking remains high (1,817 complaints over 90 days), indicating congestion vulnerability
Timing suggests possible recent change in TLC enforcement, ride-share operations, or jitney activity
reporting_angles: TLC enforcement: has ride-share compliance dropped? Are unlicensed services operating in the district?
Street congestion: interview residents about whether for-hire vehicles are blocking streets or creating traffic hazards
Economic angle: are illegal jitney services filling gap left by poor transit access (note: recurring CB request for transit elevator upgrades)
